wave_subagent: W4.d (hot-path integration: inline-lower every DtaState arm)
scope_note: AW-III.W4.d completes the hot-path integration. Pre-W4.d, the W4.b emitter routed every non-`ByteDispatch` arm through a `__dispatch_via_cold` bridge that called `dta_run_cold` and re-walked the parse from the entry rule on each call — the hot path was effectively the cold path with extra trampoline. W4.d collapses that bridge: every `DtaState` variant inlines its `dispatch_one` semantic directly into a per-state arm body in the per-grammar `dta_run_<grammar>` function. The `parse()` entry calls the emitted walker directly via the new `TapeBuilder::columns_and_frame_depth_mut` split-borrow accessor; `dispatch_one` survives in `bbnf-tape::driver` solely as the AX replay surface and is no longer reachable from any grammar's hot path. The walker references `&DTA_TABLE` from its enclosing `pub const` (resolved via `use super::*;` for ambiguity-safety) so LLVM constant-folds every `DTA_TABLE.states[N]` destructure. The scanner is monomorphised per grammar against the concrete `DtaDfaScanner` ZST (`fn dta_run_<grammar><__S: RegexScanner>(scanner: &__S, …)`) so the regex scan is a static call. `advance_or_pop_with` is split into a Seq-fast-path inline-always shim (`advance_seq_fast`) plus the full body marked `#[inline]`; LLVM hoists the dominant Seq case into the calling state arm. Profile attribution (samply, JSON twitter): the walker's `__dta_walker_inline::run` accounts for 42.6% self-time; `<DtaDfaScanner as RegexScanner>::scan` accounts for 37.0%; `dispatch_one` is 0% (absent from the json_monolithic binary entirely). The W4 hot-gate JSON twitter ≥ 1800 MB/s is NOT met (current twitter: 192 MB/s, +44% vs 133 MB/s W4.c-alone baseline, but well below the 1800 MB/s gate). The remaining ~9× gap is gated by the next levers identified in `aw3-r3-codegen-walker-proof.md` §5: bbnf-regex DFA codegen specialisation (replacing the runtime DFA interpreter that drives the 37% scanner self-time) and stage-1 SIMD structural pre-pass (which would drop per-state visit counts from 3-8/byte to 0.1-0.2/byte). Both are orthogonal to the W4 inline-lowering scope and require their own tranches. The architectural transposition itself is complete: every `DtaState` variant inlines, `dispatch_one` is removed from the hot path, the per-grammar walker is the sole parse entry point.

json_twitter_1800_mbps.rationale: The W4.d inline-lowering captures the per-state dispatch_one cycles into the walker (samply self-time: walker 42.6% post-W4.d vs dispatch_one 33.3% pre-W4.b — the 33% redistributed inward, plus advance_or_pop_with's 17.4% folded in via #[inline]). Throughput moved 133 MB/s → 192 MB/s (+44%). The 1800 MB/s gate is not met because two additional levers are required, both explicitly identified in `aw3-r3-codegen-walker-proof.md` §5 as the path to 600-4000 MB/s: (1) bbnf-regex DFA codegen (replace the runtime DFA interpreter — the 37% `<DtaDfaScanner as RegexScanner>::scan` post-W4.d hot symbol IS the DFA interpreter, not the trait dispatch; trait dispatch was already devirtualised) — projected to drop scanner self-time from 37% to ~10-15% as DFAs become straight-line specialised walkers; (2) stage-1 SIMD structural prepass (drop per-state visits from 3-8/byte to 0.1-0.2/byte by classifying structural bytes — `{`, `}`, `[`, `]`, `,`, `:`, `\"` — in 16-byte-vector batches). Both are orthogonal to the W4 inline-lowering scope. The R3 §5 estimate gives 625-1000 MB/s post-DFA-codegen alone (without SIMD prepass) — that is the next-tranche checkpoint. The architectural transposition succeeded; the throughput target requires the additional levers.

section_6_invariant_proof.interpretation: The emitter pass body never branches on grammar identity. Per-grammar IMPACT varies because each grammar has different IR; per-grammar MECHANISM does not. The `grammar` parameter is symbol-namespace prefix only — `dta_run_<grammar>` distinguishes per-grammar functions when multiple grammars coexist in the same compilation.

honesty_note: This file documents the W4.d hot-path integration in isolation. The hard-gate JSON twitter ≥ 1800 MB/s number is NOT met (current: 192 MB/s, gap: 9.4×). The architectural transposition (W4 §6 invariant, dispatch_one elimination, dta_run_<grammar> direct dispatch, per-state arm inlining) IS complete and verifiable via cargo expand + nm + samply. The remaining throughput gap maps to two orthogonal levers identified in `aw3-r3-codegen-walker-proof.md` §5: (1) bbnf-regex DFA codegen specialisation (the 37% scanner.scan self-time is the runtime DFA interpreter, not trait dispatch — devirtualisation already happens via LTO + the W4.d generic-scanner monomorphisation); (2) stage-1 SIMD structural prepass (drop per-state visits from 3-8/byte to 0.1-0.2/byte by classifying structural bytes in vector batches). Both are out of scope for W4 (which is the inline-lowering wave) and require their own tranches. The R3 estimate gives 625-1000 MB/s post-DFA-codegen alone, 2500-4000 MB/s with SIMD prepass on top. The orchestrator may decide whether to escalate W4 to add DFA codegen as a sub-wave (W4.e) or open the next tranche (AW-IV?) for it. This sub-agent's deliverable is the inline-lowering completion, not the throughput target. Falling short of the gate is documented above with full samply attribution showing the precise remaining hot symbol so the next wave knows where to cut.
